title: The Edwardian Era
description: In the 1900s, women’s fashion was defined by the Edwardian “S-bend” corset silhouette, high collars, and floor-length skirts. Outfits were ornate, with lace, puffed sleeves, and wide hats being common.

title: Transition and Simplicity
description: By the 1910s, fashion started to simplify, influenced by changing social roles and World War I. Hemlines slightly rose, corsets loosened, and dresses featured empire waists and hobble skirts.

title: The Flapper Era
description: The 1920s brought radical change with the rise of the flapper. Women wore short, straight-cut dresses with drop waists, beaded fringe, and cloche hats.

title: Hollywood Glamour
description: In the 1930s, fashion returned to elegance, influenced by Hollywood glamour. Gowns were bias-cut and flowing, with longer hemlines and a soft feminine silhouette.

title: War and Utility
description: During the 1940s, wartime rationing led to practical and tailored looks. Dresses and suits featured strong shoulders, knee-length skirts, and utility-inspired designs.

title: The Hourglass Revival
description: The 1950s saw the revival of ultra-feminine fashion with full skirts, petticoats, cinched waists, and glamorous accessories.

title: Mod and Youthquake
description: In the 1960s, youth culture exploded into fashion with mini skirts, shift dresses, and bold prints.

title: Boho and Disco
description: The 1970s embraced both bohemian and disco styles. Bell bottoms, maxi dresses, peasant tops, and jumpsuits were popular.

title: Power Dressing
description: In the 1980s, bold was better. Power dressing became a trend, with oversized blazers, shoulder pads, neon colors, and flashy accessories dominating. Fitness trends also introduced leggings and leotards into everyday wear.

title: Minimalism and Grunge
description: The 1990s embraced minimalism and grunge. Women wore slip dresses, crop tops, oversized flannels, and Doc Martens. The look was effortless and influenced by alternative music and anti-fashion statements.

title: Y2K and Flashy Trends
description: The 2000s (Y2K era) were flashy and playful with low-rise jeans, rhinestones, mini skirts, and logo-heavy brands. Pop icons inspired styles like velour tracksuits, butterfly clips, and visible midriffs.

title: Millennial Chic and Normcore
description: In the 2010s, trends from past decades reemerged—like wide-leg pants, corsets, and crop tops—while individualism, sustainability, and digital influencers shaped personal style. Comfort-focused looks like athleisure became mainstream.

title: Revival and Individualism
description: In the 2020s, fashion is highly diverse and nostalgic. Wide-leg pants, corsets, and crop tops from earlier decades have reappeared. Sustainability, digital trends, and gender-fluid styles dominate.
